flawed_step: The claimed implication from being 2-connected and Eulerian to being Hamiltonian cannot be justified.
counterexample: Let G = K_{2,4}, with bipartition A={a1,a2} and B={b1,b2,b3,b4}, and every edge ai-bj. It is finite and simple. It is connected, and all degrees are even: deg(a1)=deg(a2)=4 and deg(bj)=2. Thus G is Eulerian. It is 2-connected under the given definition: deleting a vertex of A leaves K_{1,4}, which is connected, while deleting a vertex of B leaves K_{2,3}, which is connected. But G is not Hamiltonian. Every cycle in a bipartite graph alternates between the two parts and hence contains equally many vertices from each part; a cycle through all vertices of K_{2,4} would have to contain 2 vertices from A and 4 from B, which is impossible.
assessment_summary: A proof cannot be completed because K_{2,4} is an explicit 2-connected Eulerian graph with no Hamiltonian cycle.
